turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
Turn the screen. Kids paste in from other drafts all the time. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
That's twice you've stepped around whether Owen was heard. Whatever comes of that file, nothing about this goes on his record, and nobody in his class hears a word of it.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare constantly. A bad quotation is a mistake, not proof of anything.

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.
I never said December 1. That's 4.4: Thursday, private, marked by Monday, nothing on file, and your apology for the gradebook in the same email tonight. He'll do it, to put this behind him.
Yes. Thursday, your room, nobody else in it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite this Thursday in your room, that you will mark it by Monday, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still want those dates in writing, along with your apology for entering the zero in the gradebook before anyone called me. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, marked by Monday, with nothing on his record, and she still wants the dates and your apology in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it well before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with exact dated times and answered her drafting defence by offering to check the other file's dates with her, which gave her something she could verify herself.
What cost ground: you stepped around her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero twice, which left a procedural gap she kept pressing.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the writing late on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer that in one plain sentence before you show the version history, so she has nothing procedural left to hold onto.
